summary: The famous stuff is fine — the reason to come back is the alleys you'd never find on a list of Top 10. These are the deep cuts local friends drag you to.

picks.name: JBS Jazz Kissa
picks.why: Tiny third-floor listening room with ~11,000 LPs, single owner-operator, drinks to sip while you sit silently and let the speakers cook. One of the last true jazz kissa in central Tokyo.
picks.tip: Go after 21:00 on a weeknight. Phones silent. No conversation — it's a listening bar, not a chat one.

picks.name: Omoide Yokocho (Piss Alley)
picks.why: Two narrow lanes under the JR tracks packed with 60 charcoal-smoke yakitori stalls that have been running since the post-war black market. Eight seats per stall, elbow-to-elbow, cheap beer.
picks.tip: Go with cash and a willingness to pay a ¥500 otoshi cover. The best stalls are the ones where the smoke is thickest.

picks.name: Yanaka cat walk
picks.why: One of few districts to survive WWII bombing. Narrow lanes, 1920s wooden houses, stray cats that inspired a dedicated guidebook. Stop by Neko Action shrine to the neighborhood cats.
picks.tip: Wander aimlessly between Nippori and Sendagi stations. Aim for 16:00 when Yanaka Ginza opens its croquette and yakitori shops.

picks.name: Shinjuku Golden Gai
picks.why: Six alleys, 200+ pocket-sized bars, each seating 4-8 people, themed around anything from film noir to death metal. Survivor of Tokyo's rebuilding boom.
picks.tip: Bars with an English menu pasted outside welcome tourists. Expect a ¥500-¥1,500 seat charge. Rotate bars — two drinks per stop is plenty.

picks.name: Harmonica Yokocho (Kichijoji)
picks.why: Kichijoji's post-war shopping lanes — narrow, ramshackle, lined with a mix of ancient shops and new-wave standing bars. The best evening-drink-then-walk neighborhood in western Tokyo.
picks.tip: Pair with Inokashira Park during daylight. Tachinomi Shintori (standing bar) is the reliable starter.

picks.name: Shinjuku Ni-chōme
picks.why: Asia's densest queer nightlife district — 300+ bars across a few short blocks. Historic legacy, uncomplicated welcome for any traveler regardless of orientation.
picks.tip: Aiiro Cafe (Sunday afternoons), Campy! Bar, Arty Farty — good English-friendly starters.

picks.name: Café de l'Ambre
picks.why: Opened 1948, still roasting beans aged up to 30 years, owner's recipes for siphon coffee and liqueur-laced demitasses. A sacred space for coffee obsessives.
picks.tip: Try the aged-bean pour-over. No Wi-Fi, no laptops, just the coffee.

picks.name: Daikanyama T-Site
picks.why: Three low-rise pavilions, magazine curation that makes the Strand look small, Anjin lounge upstairs for a 90-minute coffee-plus-archival-Life-magazine session. Walk-worthy any hour.
picks.tip: Go 07:00 for quiet or 22:00 for the glow. Combine with a Meguro River walk in spring.

picks.name: Nezu Jinja torii tunnel
picks.why: A quiet, walkable alternative to Kyoto's Fushimi Inari. Bright orange torii line a short hillside path at a 1,900-year-old shrine with azalea gardens peaking in late April.
picks.tip: Morning light is best for the tunnel shot. Pair with Yanaka walk — they're a 10-minute stroll apart.

picks.name: Ryogoku morning sumo practice
picks.why: Most stables open their keiko (morning practice) to outside observers during non-tournament months. Two hours of sweat, tradition, and incredible physicality a metre from your seat.
picks.tip: Arakawa Beya and a few others accept walk-ins at 06:30-09:00. Book via a guide (Magnitude Tokyo Sumo Tour) for reliable entry.

picks.name: Meguro Parasitological Museum
picks.why: Two small floors dedicated to parasites — including an 8.8-metre tapeworm on display. Free, off-beat, the exact niche Tokyo excels at.
picks.tip: Twenty-minute visit. Pair with a Meguro River walk for cherry blossom season.

picks.name: Kagurazaka lanes
picks.why: Tokyo's 'little Paris' — French bistros, geisha alleys, hidden kaiseki counters, cobbled side streets. A polished evening walk that feels like a secret.
picks.tip: Stone-paved Hyogo-yokocho and Kakurenbo-yokocho are the photogenic lanes. Early evening is the sweet spot.
